title: Session friction smoke report: slot contention probe
content:
Summary:
This is a small, informal smoke/mini-benchmark exploring session-level friction when slot contention is injected. Goal: validate that small changes to slot allocation and lightweight prefetch decrease P99 tail without blowing up amortized $/query. This doc is intentionally terse — notes-to-self style with compact text charts and action items.

Motivation/Context:
- Observability has flagged a recurring pattern: when session concurrency spikes briefly, P99 jumps more than expected relative to sustained throughput. Suspect slot contention + KV cache churn as the dominant contributors.
- We want a quick signal: if we tighten slot isolation or bias session affinity, do we get an affordable tail improvement?

Environment + config:
- Model: open-llm-v1-4b (CPU warmup suppressed, GPU T4 equivalent profile)
- Runtime: internal serving-runtime v1.13.2 (slot allocator v0.9, kv-cache opt disabled for baseline)
- Test harness: local harness + small synthetic driver that replays session traces (mixture of 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long).
- Duration: 10m per run (warmup 2m), repeated 3x per config; light random jitter in arrival times.

Workload outline:
- Session mix: short(<=30 tokens): 60%, medium(100-200 tokens): 30%, long(500-800 tokens): 10%
- Baseline concurrency: 16 sessions (sustained), with microbursts to 64 for 20s every 90s
- Metrics observed: P50/P90/P99 latency (ms), observed QPS, avg tokens per session, estimated $/1M tokens approximate using internal price model.

Configs tested:
A) baseline: shared slots, no affinity (current prod-like)
B) affinity-weak: prefer same-worker affinity (soft), reduces slot hopping by ~35%
C) isolate-small-sessions: reserve small slot pool (10%) for short sessions
D) isolate-small + affinity: combine C + B

Aggregate numeric summary (median across three runs):
Table: Concurrency=16 sustained, bursts to 64
- Config A (baseline): QPS 76 | P50 52ms | P90 170ms | P99 820ms | est $/1M tokens: $11.8
- Config B (affinity-weak): QPS 74 | P50 55ms | P90 150ms | P99 540ms | est $/1M tokens: $11.6
- Config C (reserve-small): QPS 70 | P50 50ms | P90 140ms | P99 480ms | est $/1M tokens: $12.2
- Config D (C+B): QPS 72 | P50 53ms | P90 132ms | P99 320ms | est $/1M tokens: $12.0

Interpretation notes:
- P99 improvements are largest when both session affinity and a small reserved pool are combined (Config D). Tail dropped from 820ms to 320ms (~61% reduction) with only modest QPS impact.
- Cost per token increases slightly when maintaining reserved capacity (Config C/D) but remains within a single-digit percentage of baseline (~2-4%).
- Affinity alone (B) reduces tail notably without increasing cost. Suggests slot-hopping + cold KV penalty is a substantive contributor.

Mini ASCII visualizations (for quick skimming):
- P99 vs config (lower is better):
  A: █████████████████████ (820ms)
  B: ████████████████ (540ms)
  C: ██████████████ (480ms)
  D: ██████████ (320ms)

- QPS (approx):
  A: 76 ||||||||||||||||||
  B: 74 |||||||||||||||||
  C: 70 |||||||||||||||
  D: 72 ||||||||||||||||

- $/1M tokens (normalized, baseline A=11.8):
  A: 11.8 --- baseline
  B: 11.6 (-1.7%)
  C: 12.2 (+3.4%)
  D: 12.0 (+1.7%)

Detailed observational anecdotes:
- During bursts, baseline runs show sudden increases in context load operations and concurrent KV misses; traces show short sessions tend to evict shared entries leading to higher recompute for medium sessions.
- Affinity reduces the eviction churn: we observe 30-40% fewer KV miss events per burst window.
- Reserved small-slot pool causes slight underutilization in steady-state but keeps short-session churn bounded during bursts.

Risks / caveats:
- Mini-benchmark uses synthetic traces; customer traffic may have different session length distributions and memory access patterns.
- The experiments use a single model and a single hardware profile; effects scale differently on higher capacity GPUs and for larger models where KV memory pressure is proportionally larger.
- Reserve pool sizing is sensitive: 10% was chosen heuristically; need sizing sweep.

Actionable next steps (prioritized):
1) Run a sizing sweep for reserved pool (5/10/15/20%) on 2 additional model profiles (8B and 70B quantized) — perf vs cost curve. Owner: Ravi (ticket created JIRA-OPS-1290).
2) Prototype soft-affinity as a toggle in runtime (thread-local preference + cooldown timer) and measure cold start frequency. Owner: Claire.
3) Add short-session marker in observability UI (cohort) so we can quickly measure real traffic short/medium/long mix across customers. Owner: observability infra.
4) Document a recommended conservative config for Dedicated customers who want tighter p99 SLOs (affinity + small reserve) — prepare one-pager for Solutions Eng.

Quick checklist for follow-up experiments:
- [ ] run 2x longer (30m) to capture rarer 99.9th spikes
- [ ] replay a sample of production trace (sanitized) for one tenant
- [ ] add KV miss event tagging and histogram to dashboard

Notes-to-self: keep these runs cheap and focused. If D looks consistent across models, this becomes a low-friction, high-impact knob to offer as both a Runtime flag and a Console toggle for customers trying to chase p99 SLOs.

End.
